title: PDK1 signaling in cancer: Current status and future perspectives.
authors: Honnasiddappa, Darshana Ballagere; Ramar, Mohankumar; Biju, Tincy; Sajjan, Mallikarjun; Venkatesh, Chidananda; Mahadeva, Nayan Kumar; Kunjiappan, Selvaraj; Ammunje, Damodar Nayak; Pavadai, Parasuraman
one_liner_zh: 综述PDK1在癌症中的信号调控与治疗靶向，不涉及无序蛋白、蛋白互作机制建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Dysregulation of signaling pathways governing cell growth, survival, metabolism, angiogenesis, invasion, metastasis, and therapeutic response drives cancer progression. The AGC family of kinases, such as AKT, S6K, SGK, RSK, and PKC, is important for downstream signaling. The 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase-1 protein (PDK1), encoded by the PDPK1 gene, phosphorylates activation-loop residues in these kinases and links phosphoinositide signaling to cellular growth, survival, metabolism, and transformation. The structure, regulation, cancer-associated functions, and therapeutic targeting of PDK1 are critically reviewed, with a focus on the pleckstrin homology domain, PIF pocket-mediated substrate docking, the kinase domain, and reported non-catalytic interactions. Experimental results from breast, lung, gastric, liver, hematological, and melanoma models suggest that dysregulated PDK1 signaling can increase the output of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, invasion, metabolic adaptation, and resistance to specific hormonal, chemotherapeutic, and targeted therapies. In some preclinical models, genetic suppression of PDK1 using siRNA, shRNA, or CRISPR-based methods has been shown to slow tumor cell growth and restore drug sensitivity. However, PDK1 remains an unvalidated therapeutic target in the clinic. There is no selective PDK1 inhibitor that has been clinically approved, and most pharmacological candidates are based on biochemical and cellular data. There is limited genetic evidence and in vivo evidence, and no validated clinical evidence specific to PDK1. Emerging PIF-pocket ligands, dual-site inhibitors, allosteric modulators, and protein-degradation strategies are therefore investigational strategies that need to be improved in terms of selectivity, pharmacokinetic characterization, tumor-context validation, and biomarker-guided evaluation.
abstract_zh: 调控细胞生长、存活、代谢、血管生成、侵袭、转移及治疗反应的信号通路失调驱动癌症进展。AGC家族激酶，如AKT、S6K、SGK、RSK和PKC，对下游信号传导至关重要。由PDPK1基因编码的3-磷酸肌醇依赖性蛋白激酶-1 (PDK1) 可磷酸化这些激酶中的激活环残基，并将磷酸肌醇信号传导与细胞生长、存活、代谢和转化联系起来。本文对PDK1的结构、调控、癌症相关功能及治疗靶向进行了批判性综述，重点关注pleckstrin同源结构域、PIF口袋介导的底物对接、激酶结构域以及已报道的非催化相互作用。来自乳腺癌、肺癌、胃癌、肝癌、血液肿瘤和黑色素瘤模型的实验结果表明，失调的PDK1信号可增强PI3K-AKT-mTOR通路的输出、侵袭、代谢适应以及对特定激素疗法、化疗和靶向治疗的耐药性。在一些临床前模型中，使用siRNA、shRNA或CRISPR方法对PDK1进行基因抑制已被证明可减缓肿瘤细胞生长并恢复药物敏感性。然而，PDK1在临床上仍是一个未经验证的治疗靶点。目前尚无选择性PDK1抑制剂获得临床批准，大多数药理学候选药物基于生化和细胞数据。针对PDK1的遗传学证据和体内证据有限，且缺乏经过验证的临床证据。因此，新兴的PIF口袋配体、双位点抑制剂、变构调节剂和蛋白质降解策略仍处于研究阶段，需要在选择性、药代动力学表征、肿瘤背景验证和生物标志物指导评估方面加以改进。
